questions.question_text: Three pieces of cord measure $45\text{ mm}$, $18\text{ cm}$ and $0.6\text{ m}$. What is their total length in millimetres?

options.why: Added $18$ directly as millimetres instead of converting $18\text{ cm}$ to $180\text{ mm}$.
Converted $0.6\text{ m}$ to $60\text{ mm}$ instead of $600\text{ mm}$.
Left out the $0.6\text{ m}$ piece and added only $45+180$.
Left out the $1.4\text{ m}$ side after converting the other two sides to centimetres.
Left out the $75\text{ cm}$ side and added only $140+95$.
Left out the $950\text{ mm}$ side and added only $140+75$.
Added one length and one width, $230+65$, instead of counting both pairs of sides.
Counted the two $230\text{ cm}$ lengths but omitted both $65\text{ cm}$ widths.
Counted one $230\text{ cm}$ length and both $65\text{ cm}$ widths, omitting the opposite length.
Subtracted only the $160\text{ cm}$ side from $580\text{ cm}$ and ignored the other known sides.
Subtracted $125+95$ from $580$ but omitted the known $160\text{ cm}$ side.
Added the $380\text{ cm}$ of known sides to the $580\text{ cm}$ perimeter instead of subtracting.

questions.question_text: Route $A$ is $0.35\text{ km}$, then $420\text{ m}$, then $180\text{ m}$. Route $B$ is $280\text{ m}$, then $0.46\text{ km}$, then $230\text{ m}$. Which route is shorter, and by how much?

options.why: Finds the correct $20\text{ m}$ difference but names the longer route as the shorter one.
Compares only the two sections given in kilometres, $0.46-0.35=0.11\text{ km}$, and ignores the remaining sections.
Compares only the kilometre sections to get $110\text{ m}$ AND reverses which route is shorter.

questions.question_text: A rectangular arena has perimeter $0.74\text{ km}$ and length $210\text{ m}$. What is its width?

options.why: Found the width as $160\text{ m}$ and then doubled it unnecessarily.
Subtracted one $210\text{ m}$ length from the full $740\text{ m}$ perimeter instead of halving first.
Divided the perimeter by four as if all four sides of the rectangle were equal.

questions.question_text: A five-sided garden has boundary lengths $1.6\text{ m}$, $125\text{ cm}$, $900\text{ mm}$, $1.35\text{ m}$ and $110\text{ cm}$. Edging is sold in $1.5\text{ m}$ rolls. What is the least number of rolls needed?

options.why: Rounded $6.2\div1.5=4.13\ldots$ down, leaving part of the boundary uncovered.
Rounded each side up to whole rolls separately, using $2+1+1+1+1$ rolls.
Rounded the $6.2\text{ m}$ perimeter up to $7$ without dividing by the $1.5\text{ m}$ roll length.

questions.solution_text:
$125\text{ cm}=1.25\text{ m}$
$900\text{ mm}=0.9\text{ m}$
$110\text{ cm}=1.1\text{ m}$
$P=1.6+1.25+0.9+1.35+1.1$
$=6.2\text{ m}$
$6.2\div1.5=4.13\ldots$
At least $5$ rolls are needed.
